    Changelog

    Source: NEWS.md

    cellspecR 1.2.0

    • cs_read_npy() and cs_read_npz() refuse a fixed-width string with a NUL character before its end as cellspec_error_format. Before, R stopped with the error embedded nul in string for ASCII strings. For Unicode strings with non-ASCII characters the NUL was dropped silently and the remaining characters were returned ("\0ä" was read as "ä"); such a file is now refused, which is a change in behaviour.
    • cs_read_cellspec() returns text with double quotes unchanged from tsv.gz directories. A value such as x"y in a character column (or a column name with a quote) came back as x""y, because the quote doubling of the writer was not undone; the checksums could not notice, since the file itself was intact. Existing directories are read correctly without being rewritten. Parquet storage was not affected.
    • Numeric identifiers passed to cs_new() are no longer padded with decimals when one of them is fractional: c(1, 2, 3.5) gives "1", "2", "3.5" instead of "1.0", "2.0", "3.5".
    • Readers that apply a marker_map now record the marker name used in the export: dictionary$marker_source holds it for every renamed marker and channels$channel_name keeps it, while marker carries the mapped name, as the specification describes. Both used to hold only the mapped name. A map entry that maps a marker to itself renames nothing and records nothing. cs_column_map() accepts an optional marker_source column in measurements for the same purpose.
    • The review app opens a directory written by cs_write(), as the README describes: cs_app(path = <directory>) reads it with cs_read_cellspec() and reports a failed integrity verification. Before, such a directory was rejected as a tiled export without tile tables.
    • cs_write_npy() and cs_write_npz() report a destination whose directory does not exist, or that is itself a directory, as cellspec_error_io before writing; before, the base R error “cannot open the connection” and a warning surfaced.
    • cs_read_signal_policy() reads CSV policies as text. Marker names that look like numbers or logical values ("1", "007", "TRUE") no longer fail with “invalid column types”, and min_value is restored exactly; values such as 1e-20 could come back one unit in the last place off. Hand-written files keep working: a blank fallback_compartment field means no fallback, also when other rows name one (such a mixed file used to fail), and a semicolon-separated file with decimal commas (0,5), as a spreadsheet saves it in some locales, is read as before. min_value must be written as a decimal number; other notations such as 0x10 are a cellspec_error_format.
    • cs_as_spe() keeps cells column names that are not syntactic R names, such as the Cell Type column kept by the QuPath reader. They were turned into Cell.Type, and cs_from_spe() then failed with “undefined columns selected”. cs_from_spe() also restores such names in objects converted by earlier versions and reports a missing column as cellspec_error_format.
    • cs_as_spe() and cs_as_anndata() convert objects without cells.
    • cs_read() with the default format = "auto" now selects the QuPath reader for a complete QuPath export. Its detection score, the sum of the weights 0.05, 0.25, 0.35 and 0.25, came out as 0.8999999999999999 in floating point and never reached the decisive 0.9, so automatic detection (also in the review app) failed with an ambiguity error that named a single candidate. The score is rounded and the threshold tolerates rounding.
    • plot(x, type = "marker") and the marker panel of the overview drew wrong data: every value was repeated once per cell and attributed to the wrong compartment and statistic, and memory use grew with the square of the number of cells. The plot now shows one marker with one violin per compartment and statistic, subsamples to max_points cells and names the marker in its title. Without marker it shows the first marker; before, all markers were pooled, which is the bug-fix change of that default.
    • A marker plot without finite values to draw fails with a cellspec_error_invalid error instead of a ggplot2 error at print time, and the overview leaves that panel out.
    • The centroid map uses a reversed y axis with the original coordinates in place of negated values, so axis labels match cs_cells(x)$y.
    • The plot overview places legends below its panels, and the getting-started vignette now shows the quality-control plots. Plotting needs ggplot2 3.4.0 or later; plot() says so when an older version is installed.
    • The centroid map and the cell area histogram draw one panel per image. Before, all images shared one panel, so the cells of different images lay on top of each other in the map and the histograms hid each other. The map uses one colour unless colour_by names a column; it used to colour by image_id, which the panels now show. The panels of the map, the marker plot and the area histogram follow the order of the images table (img2 before img10) and share one axis range.
    • plot() gains max_panels (default 12). With more images the panels are too small to read at the default device size, so the map, the marker plot and the area histogram pool all images in one panel and say so in the subtitle; the overview, where each view has half the width, pools above half that number. For the marker plot this changes the default for objects with more than 12 images, which used to get one unreadable panel per image; max_panels restores the panels on a larger device. Panels get fewer axis breaks, tick labels that would overprint are left out on both axes, and long image names get smaller strip labels.
    • The marker plot draws an image and source with a single cell as a point instead of warning that a violin could not be computed.
    • The support heatmap separates its tiles with white borders, lists the features from top to bottom and leaves out axis labels that would overprint their neighbours in a small panel. Discrete map colours stop before the yellow end of the viridis scale, which is hard to see on white.
    • The examples of plot() now draw every plot on the reference page; only the last one was shown. The adapter article lists the readers as a table, and the performance article shows the recorded measurements instead of a placeholder. The README starts with its title; the table of contents above it is gone.
    • Review app: the package name stands next to the logo in the title bar, the map is drawn larger and at 96 dpi with a text alternative, and the About panel no longer puts spaces before its full stops. The app needs shiny 1.6.0 or later.
    • x[0, ] and x[, 0] now select no cells and no features, as in base R. Zero positions used to select everything, so an empty selection silently returned the complete object. Zeros mixed with other positions are ignored.
    • When replacement and automatic restoration both fail, report the retained original backup directory explicitly so it can be recovered before retrying.
    • Schema columns must be plain vectors of their declared type. Matrix, array, factor and other classed columns are rejected before downstream use. The canonical writer applies the same rule to extra metadata columns, preventing matrix columns from being silently truncated during TSV output.
    • Detect native symbolic links, dangling links and Windows junctions without relying on the Windows Sys.readlink() stub; retain manifest and overwrite boundaries across platforms.
    • Preserve existing NumPy files when input validation fails. Decode signed and unsigned integer boundaries exactly in both byte orders, including int32 minimum and 64-bit integers in the supported range +/-2^53. Reject duplicate archive names and unsupported array dimensions.
    • Recheck overwrite permission and destination contents immediately before committing canonical writes; refuse symbolic-link destinations and members. This protects late-arriving unrelated files, but is not a concurrent-writer lock.
    • Include hidden files in integrity verification and refuse symlink members and unsafe portable manifest paths. Checksums establish consistency, not authorship.
    • Treat external parser diagnostics as literal text so braces cannot be evaluated as formatting expressions and structured error classes survive.
    • Reject partial delimited reads with parser warnings, preserve leading-zero and large integer identifiers, and reject lossy sidecar integer conversions. Use unambiguous composite cell keys even when identifiers contain separators.
    • The review app retains upload filenames for RDS/gzip dispatch and image identity, and clears review results when inputs change or a read fails.
    • AnnData documentation and examples use the native R in-memory backend; interoperability tests now require successful conversion when installed.
    • Prepare the first CRAN submission: print snapshots no longer embed the package version, and the version is aligned across DESCRIPTION, CITATION.cff, .zenodo.json and the README.

    cellspecR 1.1.0

    • Functions released in 1.0.0 are no longer marked experimental; like the package, they are stable. The NumPy readers and writers added in this version are experimental.

    • The MCQuant, segmantR and inForm readers derive image and sample identifiers of an RDS table from its file name, as for delimited files; before, they came from a temporary copy and differed between reads.

    • Standardize the named v5 package logo across README, documentation pages and available application headers, with matching light and dark artwork.

    • cs_read_npy() and cs_read_npz() read NumPy array files and archives in base R (booleans, integers, floats, complex, fixed-width strings; C or Fortran order); cs_write_npy() and cs_write_npz() write them without an external zip program.

    • Signal policies can declare separate preferred and fallback finite domains, including negative finite measurements. Existing minimum-domain defaults and five-column policies remain unchanged. Extended seven-column policies preserve both domains through JSON and CSV.

    • Signal-policy I/O preserves structured error classes when parser diagnostics or paths contain literal braces.

    • Canonical TSV decimal conversion now preserves double precision on platforms where extended precision equals double precision, including macOS ARM. The 17-digit file format and exact-value round-trip contract are unchanged.

    • Header-only TSV exports now write a complete gzip stream, including empty cell and adjacency tables. Their declared column types survive read-back.

    • QuPath readers recognize compartment-first cell area and nuclear morphology with explicit units. Whole-cell area is kept separately from nuclear area; shape dictionaries retain the original headers and dimensional units.

    • The segmantR reader converts one-based pixel-index centroid means to the image’s pixel-edge coordinate frame and converts pixel area to square micrometres. Unrecognised centroid conventions are rejected. Crop, pyramid and anisotropic transforms must be handled explicitly before image integration. Raw shape measurements retain their pixel or radian units.

    • cs_formats() reports segmantR 0.2.0, the version the segmantR reader was tested with, instead of the non-existent segmantR 0.5.

    • cs_write(overwrite = TRUE) now replaces only an empty directory or earlier cs_write() output: a directory whose cellspec.json carries the cellspec format marker and which holds no files other than those cs_write() creates. Any other directory is left untouched and an error names the unexpected entries.

    • Tiled QuPath done markers with header_sha256 now verify header lines longer than 1,024 bytes instead of reporting a missing header, and check the decompressed header line of gzip-compressed (.gz) tiles instead of their compressed bytes.

    • cs_app() now applies max_upload_mb as the Shiny upload limit while the application runs and restores the previous limit when it stops; uploads were previously capped at the 5 MB Shiny default.

    • The default plot() overview leaves out the area panel when the cells table has no area column and the marker panel when there are no intensity features, instead of failing.

    • cs_as_anndata() now defaults to policy = NULL and derives the policy the same way as cs_as_spe().

    • other features whose source names clean to the same identifier are numbered with make.unique(sep = "_") instead of aborting the read. This covers unmapped numeric columns kept by keep_other = TRUE and measurements mapped with kind = "other", also with keep_other = FALSE. Suffixes already in use are skipped: columns “a b”, “a_b” and “a_b_1” become other:a_b, other:a_b_2 and other:a_b_1.

    • summary() and its print method handle valid objects without images.

    • cs_read_cellspec() checks the row counts declared in cellspec.json before reading and reports a missing or malformed n_rows as a cellspec_error_format.

    • cs_write() no longer advances the session random number generator when it names its staging and backup directories.

    • Gzip-compressed tables and canonical tsv.gz files are decompressed in R on every platform instead of through an external gzip program. The result is checked against the gzip trailer (CRC-32 and length), so a truncated or corrupt file raises a cellspec_error_format instead of loading only part of its rows. A file whose tail was zero-filled back to its original size counts as truncated. BGZF files (bgzip) are checked block by block, may hold nothing but BGZF blocks and must end with the BGZF end-of-file block; other files made of several gzip members, which cannot be checked completely, are read with a cellspec_warning_integrity warning.

    • cellspecR now requires data.table 1.17.0 or later. Earlier versions write fwrite(compress = "gzip") output as several gzip members, which cs_read_cellspec() cannot fully check, so it would warn on the tsv.gz files written by cs_write().

    cellspecR 1.0.0

    First public release, on GitHub.

    Specification

    • Added the cellspec 1.0 table contract, JSON Schema and vocabulary tables for segmented cells from multiplexed tissue images.

    Readers

    • Added readers for QuPath, tiled QuPath, MCQuant, segmantR, inForm and mapped generic CSV/TSV tables, with format detection and provenance records.

    Validation

    • Added structural and semantic validation, actionable reports, feature support summaries and deterministic synthetic examples.

    Canonical format

    • Added Parquet storage with an exact text fallback, JSON sidecars, SHA-256 manifests, completion markers and atomic staging.

    Signals

    • Added explicit signal policies, marker maps and selected signal matrices with JSON and CSV persistence.

    Interoperability

    • Added guarded conversion to and from SpatialExperiment and AnnData objects.

    Methods

    • Added tile binding and merge helpers, cellspec subsetting and coercion, and quality-control map, marker, support, area and overview plots.

    Interactive front-end

    • Added a local Shiny review app for reading exports, inspecting validation and downloading review tables.
